analysis:
All four units are documentation-only changes (docs/provider/cli-reference.md and docs/provider/troubleshooting.md). No source code, key handling, attestation, wire protocol or authorization logic changes in these units, so there is no direct security regression.

What the docs describe:
- The shutdown drain now waits up to 15 s per model unload (`ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown`). A model whose native retirement never finishes is left to process exit. This touches TB-007/T-010/T-029 availability and T-028 residual GPU data. It is a documented lifecycle behavior only, and I could not verify the implementation from the supplied text.
- A drain with no coordinator session needs no acknowledgement. This is a lifecycle availability point and does not weaken the A-016/T-053 authorization semantics. The coordinator-side contract is platform-owned and not in the supplied evidence.
- New status lines: `Retrying <model> when memory frees` and `Configuration change needs a restart to apply: enabled_models`. They record `enabled_models_at_start` and `enabled_models_at_last_switch` in the daemon state file. These are local, non-secret operational fields and expose no prompts, keys or tokens. The retry path unloads only idle models outside the selection. I could not verify that eviction cannot touch in-flight or Autopilot-held models, but the docs say it does not.
- The cli-reference head text lines 2125-2372 are mostly unchanged context. They include the sandbox add-on path (TB-013/T-061), the App Attest worker env passthrough (TB-011), and the prefix-cache and SSD env variables (T-041). I saw no change that widens T-041 scope, TTL or storage. The documented 30-minute sliding TTL and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gating are consistent with the canonical T-041.

Open questions for integration: the code behind the described drain/retry behavior (ProviderLoop, ServiceDrain) is not in this batch. The new Autopilot-style automatic reload, and its interaction with the add-on hold (TB-012/T-059) and model-load fences, should be checked if the code ships in the same PR.
